subject: Auto Electrical Work
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice questions in 45 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2: six short-structured questions, answer any four, in 1 hour for 60 marks. Paper 3: practical test of 2 hours, three skill-based questions of which two are answered, for 90 marks (a theoretical alternative of two compulsory essay questions in 2 hours for 100 marks may be set). Industrial attachment between SS II and SS III is assessed by subject teachers for 10 marks.

subtopics.name: Concept of battery
objectives: Define a battery and distinguish a motor vehicle battery from other batteries

subtopics.name: Uses of battery
objectives: State the uses of a battery, including vehicle battery assembly and as a power source in soldering

subtopics.name: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
objectives: Describe the lead-acid and nickel-alkaline types, their construction and ratings

subtopics.name: Charging of battery
objectives: Observe safety rules in charging
Prepare electrolyte
Clean and connect batteries
Describe charging mode and state of charge

subtopics.name: Testing and maintenance of battery
objectives: Carry out electrolyte testing: specific gravity test, cell voltage and polarity tests
Use the tools and equipment for testing and maintenance
Top up electrolyte, read and interpret a hydrometer, recognise over-charging symptoms and apply safe-keeping of an idle battery

subtopics.name: Purpose and components of starting system
objectives: State the purpose of the starting system
Identify its components: battery, flywheel, starter motor, switch and solenoid

subtopics.name: Circuit diagram of starting system
objectives: Draw and read the circuit diagram
Locate the components and their sequential arrangement in a vehicle

subtopics.name: Types of starter motor
objectives: Distinguish the axial and inertia types of starter motor
Describe pinion engagements

subtopics.name: Repair of starter motors
objectives: Dismantle and assemble a starter motor
Replace bushings and brushes
Repair or solder the commutator
Troubleshoot and rectify faults
Service the armature and diagnose and restore faults

subtopics.name: Purpose and components of ignition system
objectives: Describe the ignition system assembly
Identify the circuit cables, ignition switch, battery, coil, distributor, capacitor, high tension leads and sparking plugs

subtopics.name: Circuit diagram of ignition system
objectives: Draw and read the circuit diagram, including line diagram and conventional symbols

subtopics.name: Construction and operation of ignition coil
objectives: Describe the internal construction and operation of the ignition coil

subtopics.name: Types of ignition system
objectives: Distinguish the conventional contact breaker and electronic ignition systems

subtopics.name: Ignition timing
objectives: Explain ignition timing and timing faults such as retarded ignition and over-advanced ignition

subtopics.name: Ignition faults and repairs
objectives: Diagnose faults such as hard starting, jerking and back firing
Use a multimeter, scanner, test lamps etc. in fault finding

subtopics.name: Purpose and components of charging system
objectives: Describe the charging system assembly as a sub-system in a motor vehicle
Identify its components: switch, battery, cables, alternators, voltage regulators

subtopics.name: Alternator
objectives: Describe the constructional details of an alternator
Explain conversion of a.c. to d.c. (rectification)
State the function of each part of an alternator

subtopics.name: Circuit diagram of charging system
objectives: Draw and read the circuit diagram, using graphical and pictorial representation
Explain the need for diagrammatic representation
Remove and fix the charging system units

subtopics.name: Charging system faults and repairs
objectives: Replace brushes and bearings
Test, repair and replace diodes
Deal with faults such as bearing seizure and charging failure

subtopics.name: Purpose and classification of lighting in a motor vehicle
objectives: State the purpose of lighting and distinguish obligatory and non-obligatory lights

subtopics.name: Head lamps
objectives: Identify the types and features of head lamps
Set head lamps

subtopics.name: Circuit diagram of lighting system
objectives: Classify, draw and read the circuit diagram
Troubleshoot the lighting system

subtopics.name: Maintenance and repairs of lighting system
objectives: Use tools, equipment and procedures to repair faults such as broken headlamp lens, bulb failure, non-aligned headlamps, open and short circuits

subtopics.name: Concept and components of auxiliary system
objectives: Define the auxiliary system, its uses and units
Explain the needs for the auxiliary system

subtopics.name: Constructional details and operation of auxiliary system components
objectives: Describe the water temperature gauge, oil pressure gauge, fuel gauge, horn relay, wiper switch, screen washer pump, indicator and door switch

subtopics.name: Maintenance and repairs of auxiliary components
objectives: Troubleshoot auxiliary components
Use tools, equipment and procedures to repair faults such as failure of horn, screen wiper, oil pressure gauge and fuel gauge
